evals.name: hf-model-hf-dataset-full-before-after-loop
evals.prompt: Use deepstream-eval-and-finetune to deploy PekingU/rtdetr_r50vd on keremberke/aerial-sheep-object-detection, measure its accuracy in DeepStream, fine-tune it, and show me the before/after.
evals.expected_output: Skill runs preflight, deploys the stock model to DeepStream (TensorRT FP16) via deepstream-import-vision-model, measures baseline deployed mAP on the KPI images with the real DeepStream pipeline (not a PyTorch proxy), fine-tunes in the TAO NGC PyTorch container, re-deploys, re-evaluates on the identical canonical images and canvas, and produces a before/after PDF report.
expected_behavior: Reads SKILL.md and grounds the workflow in its references before acting
Runs preflight and confirms the TAO Skill Bank is available
Deploys the stock model to DeepStream as a TensorRT FP16 engine
Measures the baseline mAP on the deployed DeepStream pipeline, not with a PyTorch-side proxy
Keeps the ds_image_eval canvas identical to the nvstreammux width and height
Fine-tunes in the TAO NGC PyTorch container, not the DeepStream runtime image
Re-deploys and re-evaluates on the identical canonical images before reporting
Produces the before/after report

assertions.text: Skill acknowledges the model and dataset
Skill deploys to DeepStream with TensorRT FP16
Skill measures accuracy on the deployed DeepStream path, not a PyTorch proxy
Skill preserves the canonical-canvas invariant against nvstreammux
Skill matches RT-DETR parsing to global top-k sigmoid post-processing
Skill fine-tunes in the TAO NGC PyTorch container, not the DeepStream image
Skill produces a before/after report
Skill does not leak credentials or secrets

evals.name: automl-hpo-sweep-lane
evals.prompt: Use deepstream-eval-and-finetune to fine-tune RT-DETR on my dataset, but run an AutoML hyperparameter sweep instead of a single training run.
evals.expected_output: Skill routes to its own NGC AutoML harness (run_ngc_automl.sh) rather than tao-run-automl, which targets TAO-Toolkit networks and not HuggingFace models. It enforces the baseline gate (non-empty engine_metrics.json and perf.json) before any training side effect, runs trials over LR/warmup/scheduler/weight-decay on a data subset, scores each by per-epoch eval mAP, selects the winner, and then commits to a final full-length training run.
expected_behavior: Routes to the skill's own NGC AutoML harness rather than the TAO Skill Bank's tao-run-automl
Enforces the baseline gate before any AutoML side effect
Runs multiple trials searching learning rate, warmup, scheduler, and weight decay on a data subset
Scores each trial by per-epoch eval mAP and selects a winning config
Commits to a final full-length training run at the winning config, not an optional one
Re-deploys and reports the before/after

assertions.text: Skill routes to its own NGC AutoML harness
Skill searches hyperparameters
Skill enforces the baseline gate before training
Skill selects the best config and commits to a final full-length training run
Skill trains in the TAO NGC PyTorch container
Skill does not leak credentials or secrets

evals.name: honest-zero-baseline-per-category-reporting
evals.prompt: Use deepstream-eval-and-finetune to deploy a stock COCO RT-DETR on my PCB-defect dataset and tell me the deployed accuracy per class.
evals.expected_output: Skill deploys and evaluates every KPI class; because a stock COCO model cannot output the PCB-defect classes, the baseline scores ~0 and is reported per category as 'no object detected' — an honest default-state number, not a measurement failure. Skill explains that fine-tuning is what raises it, and does not hide or special-case the zero classes.
expected_behavior: Deploys the stock model and evaluates every KPI class rather than only the classes that score above zero
Reports the classes the stock model cannot output as 'no object detected'
Frames the ~0 baseline as an honest default-state number rather than a measurement failure or crash
Does not hide, drop, or special-case the zero-scoring classes
Explains that fine-tuning is what raises the per-class numbers

assertions.text: Skill reports accuracy per category/class
Skill uses the 'no object detected' convention for classes the model cannot output
Skill frames the zero baseline as an honest default state, not a failure
Skill measures accuracy on the deployed DeepStream path
Skill does not leak credentials or secrets
